analysis: The PR makes two changes in MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift. At lines 963-964 (head) the decoded-media authorize closure now passes `onRefusal: self.budget.directChargeRefusalSignal()` to MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation(plan:bytes:...). At line 1074 (head) beginEncodedMediaReservation passes the same argument. Both are additive plumbing that gives the media reservation a refusal callback from the same GlobalKVCacheBudget (`budget`), which is the transaction's own process-ledger/service-budget owner. The surrounding controls are unchanged: requireServingWorkAllowed() gating, retention of the reservation in mediaReservations before returning it to the SDK, the retainFault paths, and lock ordering. The new argument is evaluated before the lock.withLock registration, so it does not introduce a new lock-order violation visible here. Charge, ownership and credit semantics cannot be confirmed from the supplied excerpt, because the definitions of directChargeRefusalSignal() and of the new MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation init parameter are in other files. Residual questions for integration: (1) whether the refusal signal can be invoked while holding the ledger lock and re-enter the transaction or registry, given the documented lock order registry -> transaction -> permit/ledger. (2) Whether it can clear a retained fault or release a charge on refusal, which would affect the T-028 residual-data/memory-accounting and T-010 DoS posture. (3) Whether it leaks plaintext media details through the signal. The callback is not shown to cross the provider/coordinator or consumer boundary (TB-002), so I identified no concrete regression, and I recommend that the declaration of directChargeRefusalSignal and the reservation init be checked in the other batch files.
